correctness.rationale: For arbitrary coprime positive a,d and b>=2, all proposed binomials balance degrees. Repeated replacement Y^(b+1)->X^bZ preserves T and lowers y; other replacements lower nonnegative T by a. Final pairs (y,z) uniquely enumerate T=0,...,a-1, so equal semigroup degrees have equal final monomials by gcd(a,d)=1; this proves generation. Removing any displayed relation leaves its no-X left monomial disconnected from its paired factorization under other moves, proving minimality. The low two-generator range follows by explicit elimination and gcd(A,B)=1. Each exponent is positive where required; the high-range minimality of A,B,C and Betti-degree inequalities are verified. The bundled finite checker tested 1320 parameter sets and 2294527 monomials, plus relation omission graphs; enumeration is explicitly not used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The two closest 2023 manuscripts prove generalized affine-repunit Frobenius/genus/Apéry formulas but do not state these exact defining-ideal generators or the complete-intersection arithmetic boundary. Explicit 2022–23 minimal resolution papers concern a distinct repunit-fixed first generator, with overlap on special instances only. General embedding-dimension-three semigroup methods exist and can in principle recover instances; no located general theorem gave the claimed direct formulas across arbitrary coprime a,d. Searches in the mathematical finding index and targeted public literature did not yield dominating coverage. Novelty remains contingent on unindexed algebraic literature. A further comparison used the equivalent generators <a,a+c,a+(b+1)c> and the 2003 Maloo–Sengupta criterion for almost-arithmetic sequences; that work gives a general framework, not these explicit generator-degree formulas.

value.rationale: The published 2023 arithmetic family has exact Frobenius and genus results but lacks a complete explicit minimal toric presentation. Relations among its three generators and their Betti degrees are natural factorization invariants; here they are uniformly classified in three sharply separated regimes. In particular, the complete-intersection transition at divisibility by b+1 and the full three Betti degrees for nondivisible cases are structural, nontrivial and useful for future homological/factorization studies. The result holds for every a,b,d in a natural infinite class rather than arbitrary tiny cases.
